subtopics.title: Newton's First Law and the Meaning of Inertia

questions.question: Newton's first law says an object continues at rest or at uniform velocity in a straight line unless acted on by:
options: Any force at all
A net or unbalanced force
Gravity
Friction

questions.question: Inertia is best described as:
options: The force that keeps an object moving forward
The energy stored in a moving object
The tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion
The friction between an object and the road

questions.question: A taxi brakes hard and a passenger lunges forward. The correct explanation is:
options: A forward force acts on the passenger during braking
The passenger's inertia pushes them into the seat
The brakes act on the passenger before they act on the taxi
A backward force slows the taxi, but no such force acts on the passenger, who continues at the original velocity

questions.question: Which object requires NO net force for its motion?
options: A car rounding a bend at constant speed
A puck gliding across frictionless ice at constant velocity
A crate accelerating across a floor
A rocket rising faster and faster

subtopics.title: Newton's Second Law and the Fnet = ma Method

questions.question: A 25 kg crate is pulled with 120 N against 45 N of friction. Its acceleration is:
options: 3 m·s⁻² in the direction of the pull
4,8 m·s⁻² in the direction of the pull
1,8 m·s⁻² backward
6,6 m·s⁻² in the direction of the pull

questions.question: The same crate must now move at constant velocity. The required pull is:
options: 0 N

questions.question: One newton is defined as:
options: The weight of one kilogram on Earth
The net force giving 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m·s⁻²
The force of gravity at sea level
One kilogram metre per second

questions.question: Which step does NOT belong in the Fnet = ma method?
options: Draw a free-body diagram with labelled arrows
Choose and state a positive direction
Add the object's weight into the horizontal equation
Substitute and state the answer with unit and direction

subtopics.title: Vertical Applications — Lifts, Cables and Apparent Weight

questions.question: A 60 kg learner stands on a scale in a lift accelerating upward at 1,5 m·s⁻². The scale reads:
The same lift now accelerates downward at 1,5 m·s⁻². The scale reads:
options: 0 N

questions.question: If the lift cable snaps and the lift falls freely, the scale reads zero because:
options: Gravity stops acting inside a falling lift
The learner's mass becomes zero
The supporting force vanishes while gravity still acts — apparent weightlessness
The scale breaks under the extra load

questions.question: An 8 000 kg rocket produces 100 000 N of thrust. Its lift-off acceleration is:
options: 12,5 m·s⁻² upward
2,7 m·s⁻² upward
9,8 m·s⁻² upward
21 600 m·s⁻² upward

subtopics.title: Newton's Third Law and Action-Reaction Pairs

questions.question: Newton's third law states that when A exerts a force on B, then B exerts on A a force that is:
options: Equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
Smaller, because some force is lost
Equal and in the same direction
Opposite in direction but always weaker

questions.question: Which property is essential for a genuine action-reaction pair?
options: Both forces act on the same object
The two forces act on different objects
One force must be gravitational
The forces must act at different times

questions.question: A dictionary rests on a desk. The reaction pair to the dictionary's weight is:
options: The desk pushing the dictionary up
The friction between dictionary and desk
The dictionary pulling the Earth upward
The desk pushing the floor down

questions.question: The donkey pulls the cart, and the cart pulls back equally. The cart still accelerates because:
options: The donkey's pull is actually slightly bigger
Friction cancels the cart's backward pull
The third law only applies at constant velocity
The two pulls act on different objects, so they never appear in the same net-force equation

subtopics.title: Why You Jerk Forward When the Taxi Brakes

questions.question: When the taxi brakes suddenly, your body moves toward the seat in front because:
options: Your body keeps its original forward velocity while the taxi slows
The brakes push your body forward
Air inside the taxi pushes you forward
Gravity acts forward during braking

questions.question: A full water bucket is harder to start and stop than an empty one because it has more:
options: Friction
Mass, and therefore more inertia
Weight, and therefore less inertia
Speed

questions.question: The seatbelt's job, in first-law language, is to:
options: Keep you comfortable in your seat
Reduce the taxi's braking distance
Supply the backward force your body needs so it slows together with the taxi
Increase your inertia during a crash

questions.question: The only force an object's acceleration responds to is:
options: The applied force alone
The largest single force
The friction force
The net (leftover) force after opposing forces are subtracted

questions.question: A rope pulls a 25 kg crate with 120 N while friction claws back 45 N. Each kilogram of crate receives:
options: 3 newtons of leftover push, giving a = 3 m·s⁻²
4,8 newtons of leftover push, giving a = 4,8 m·s⁻²
75 newtons of leftover push
120 newtons of leftover push

questions.question: A question says an object moves at constant velocity. You should immediately write:
options: Fnet = ma with a = 9,8
The net force is zero, so all forces balance
The applied force is zero
The object has no inertia

questions.question: Doubling the mass while keeping the same net force will:
options: Double the acceleration
Leave the acceleration unchanged
Halve the acceleration
Quarter the acceleration

subtopics.title: The Lift Floor and the Wall That Pushes Back

questions.question: A bathroom scale in a lift actually measures:
options: Your mass in kilograms
The gravitational force of the Earth on the lift
Your inertia
The upward push the scale exerts on your feet

questions.question: During all the lift readings — 678 N, 588 N, 498 N, 0 N — the learner's true weight:
options: Never changed at all
Changed with each reading
Was zero in free fall
Equalled the scale reading each time

questions.question: Walking forward is possible because:
options: Your muscles push your body directly forward
You push the ground backward and the ground pushes you forward
Friction always acts in the direction of motion
Your inertia pulls you toward your destination

questions.question: Weight down and normal force up on a resting dictionary are NOT an action-reaction pair because:
options: They are not equal in size
They act in the same direction
They both act on the same object and are different types of force
The normal force acts only while the dictionary moves
